assessments.operationalization: Use genomic parentage and reproductive records to test wolf-dog and fox-dog crosses and the ancestry of Laconian-type hounds. Hybrid genomes support a cross; incompatible chromosome biology or dog-only ancestry refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public canid genome and sequence data

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public canid DNA barcode records

obstacles: The historical Laconian hound population may not have surviving representatives.
assessments.rationale: Wolf-dog hybridization and canid ancestry are directly resolvable from extensive genetic data. The exact extinct or transformed dog lineage is harder, but the fox-dog biological assertion is strongly testable.

assessments.operationalization: Compare known-age fish with scale radius, annuli and quantified hardness across species. Predictive age accuracy above chance supports the claim; systematic age mismatch refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish age, growth and scale-aging references

obstacles: Modern scale aging relies mainly on annuli rather than hardness.
Accuracy varies among species and older ages.
assessments.rationale: Scale-based age estimation is a standard fisheries method with abundant validation data. The specific hardness component is less routinely digitized, but size and scale structure allow the core claim to be assessed.

assessments.operationalization: Choose pre-registered behavioral measures of risk-taking and aggression as 'spirit', estimate sex differences species by species, and compare bears and leopards with the distribution. Numerous female-lower exceptions would refute universality.
obstacles: Courage has several non-equivalent operationalizations.
Sex-specific behavioral data are taxonomically sparse.
Ecological and reproductive context strongly confound comparisons.
assessments.rationale: Some measurable proxies permit restricted tests, especially aggression or boldness within well-studied species. They cannot preserve the full ancient concept or support a generalization over all sexually reproducing animals.

assessments.operationalization: Model antagonistic interaction frequency against spatial and dietary overlap, and within species compare fighting under low versus high food availability. Positive controlled associations support both clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: open antagonistic and trophic species-interaction records

obstacles: Co-occurrence and diet overlap do not imply enmity.
Interaction records are highly biased toward conspicuous taxa.
assessments.rationale: Large public occurrence and interaction resources allow comparative tests, but causality is confounded by shared habitat, abundance and phylogeny. Experimental food-shortage evidence covers only selected species.

assessments.operationalization: Compare fear and aggression in replicated wild-animal populations under sustained unlimited versus normal food while controlling human exposure. Persistent wildness despite food abundance would refute the prediction.
obstacles: Unlimited food is an unrealized counterfactual.
Provisioning co-varies with habituation to humans.
Wild and tame require behavioral thresholds.
assessments.rationale: The prediction has observable consequences, but existing provisioning observations cannot isolate food abundance from repeated human contact and selection. A decisive general test would require new controlled longitudinal data.

assessments.operationalization: Use known-age red deer photographs and specimens to model antler points and complexity from ages one through older adulthood. The exact annual sequence and loss of age discrimination after six are direct predictions.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public deer skeletal specimens and scans

obstacles: Most public images lack known individual age.
Nutrition and condition strongly affect antler form.
assessments.rationale: The morphology-age relation is explicit and deer-management studies contain known-age samples. Open, harmonized individual-level age data are incomplete, so the exact schedule is only partly resolvable from public datasets.

assessments.operationalization: Review continuous birth observations of red deer and record whether, when and how often the hind consumes the placenta before it reaches the ground. Any observed non-consumption refutes the invariant wording.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public wildlife video potentially documenting deer parturition

obstacles: Wild births are rarely observed continuously.
Publication and video selection favor unusual events.
assessments.rationale: The behavior is unambiguous and individual observations can confirm occurrence or provide counterexamples. Existing public observations are too few and biased to estimate how invariant it is.

assessments.operationalization: For dogs, link illness status, grass ingestion and subsequent vomiting in time-stamped veterinary or owner records, comparing with healthy controls. Increased grass eating before vomiting supports the stated example but not intentional treatment.
obstacles: Intentional self-treatment is not directly observable.
Public linked clinical-behavioral records are sparse.
Grass eating also occurs in healthy dogs.
assessments.rationale: The sequence in dogs is measurable from existing studies, but the functional and intentional interpretation has weak discriminating power. The broad claim about many quadrupeds has little standardized coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Identify candidate trochilus species and review georeferenced video and field observations for entry into Nile-crocodile mouths, food removal and crocodile tolerance. Authenticated repeated events support the claim; intensive observation without them weighs against it.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird behavior media

obstacles: The bird's modern identity is disputed.
Absence of a rare interaction is difficult to establish.
assessments.rationale: The interaction has clear visual consequences and public media can expose supporting events or misidentifications. No systematic dataset samples crocodile mouths enough to establish typicality.

assessments.operationalization: Use individually marked pigeons and genetic parentage to estimate pair-bond duration, re-pairing before partner death and extra-pair mating. Any surviving-partner re-pairing tests the strict life-pair clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open individual bird tracking datasets

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public pigeon genetic resources supporting parentage studies

obstacles: Tracking locations do not by themselves identify mating.
Wild lifetime histories are often censored by disappearance.
assessments.rationale: Pair bonds and genetic mating are standard ornithological outcomes with existing studies. Public longitudinal coverage is adequate for populations, but disappearance makes a literal lifetime statement difficult.

assessments.operationalization: Code nest architecture and flight capacity for quails, partridges and comparable ground birds. Constructed nests refute the first clause; comparative models test whether reduced flight predicts simpler nests.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public nest and breeding-behavior media

obstacles: A scraped lined hollow may qualify as a nest.
The proposed usefulness is an adaptive explanation with alternative causes.
assessments.rationale: Nest type and flight ability are well documented for the named birds, allowing direct resolution of the empirical clause. The final-cause wording has lower discriminating power but predicts a testable association.

assessments.operationalization: Review predator- or human-approach observations of nesting partridges and quails for injury-feigning, displacement direction, chick escape and reunion calls. Repeated complete sequences support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird behavior video and audio

obstacles: The full sequence is rarely captured.
Observer-triggered records may be biased and ethically constrained.
assessments.rationale: Distraction displays are standard observable behavior and substantial public media and literature exist. Completeness and frequency across the stated taxa remain only partly represented.

assessments.operationalization: Classify web-footed species and calculate their occurrence distances from marine and inland waters. Repeated populations far from water refute the universal association.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: fine-scale habitat use by tracked waterbirds

obstacles: Near requires a pre-specified distance threshold.
assessments.rationale: Foot morphology, taxonomy and habitat occurrence are richly documented in public data. A spatial analysis can test the universal claim globally within weeks.

assessments.operationalization: Collect age, health, time-to-death, location and vocalization rates from individually monitored swans, testing whether song increases near death and whether birds move offshore. Existing recordings lacking life outcome cannot decide the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public swan vocal recordings and observation metadata

obstacles: Public recordings are not linked to subsequent death.
Musical and mournful are subjective.
Rare terminal events create severe selection bias.
assessments.rationale: The mortality-linked prediction is measurable, but available sound archives do not follow individuals to death. A decisive analysis needs new longitudinal monitoring despite abundant ordinary swan recordings.

assessments.operationalization: Compile monitored common-cuckoo nesting attempts, clutch size, incubation and host care. Any self-built nest, multi-egg laying event or maternal incubation refutes the corresponding universal clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public cuckoo and host nesting media

obstacles: One female's eggs across several host nests must not be mistaken for a clutch in one nest.
assessments.rationale: Brood parasitism is exceptionally well studied and the behavioral variables are direct. Public observations and published datasets can resolve each clause with high power.

assessments.operationalization: Boldness and nest-defense could be measured, but no observation distinguishes conscious cowardice as the purpose of brood parasitism from evolutionary and ecological alternatives.
obstacles: Conscious awareness of cowardice is inaccessible.
The final-cause explanation makes no unique observable prediction.
assessments.rationale: Cuckoo defense behavior can be compared with other birds, but that proxy does not resolve the stated mental and purposive cause. Any outcome can be redescribed as compatible with the story, giving it little discriminating power.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate eagle pair home ranges, food requirements, juvenile dispersal and neighboring-bird density from telemetry and surveys. Larger energetic needs predicting broader territories and active exclusion supports the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open eagle movement, territory and dispersal data

obstacles: Low nearby bird density can result from habitat rather than expulsion.
Eagles comprises many species.
assessments.rationale: Home range and juvenile dispersal are well represented in telemetry data, and energetic requirements are estimable. Directly attributing all neighboring-bird absence to active exclusion is more confounded, but the mechanism has testable predictions.

assessments.operationalization: Continuously video-monitor identified sea-eagle nests before fledging and score forced sun orientation, beating, eye watering and chick mortality. Absence across adequate samples or survival of affected chicks refutes the sequence.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public sea-eagle and osprey nesting media

obstacles: Existing public media are not a systematic continuous sample.
Sea-eagle identification is ambiguous.
The claimed event may be extremely rare.
assessments.rationale: The alleged actions are visually explicit, but no known open dataset samples the critical episodes with sufficient coverage. New standardized nest-camera annotation or collection is needed.

assessments.operationalization: Use anatomical records and feeding video of Lophius to test illicial filament position, prey attraction, contact and capture while concealed. Videos showing the complete lure-to-capture sequence confirm the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: anglerfish anatomy, diet and behavior references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anglerfish anatomical specimens and scans

obstacles: In situ predation videos are less numerous than anatomical records.
assessments.rationale: The lure and its use are concrete, distinctive traits documented in comparative anatomy and behavior. Existing public data can resolve both structure and function.

assessments.operationalization: Measure electric-organ discharges from Torpedo rays and prey or human neuromuscular responses, linking discharge to capture events. A body-generated discharge preceding prey immobilization directly supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: electric-ray biology and referenced electrophysiology

assessments.rationale: Electrical discharge and prey stunning are directly measurable and extensively established in public scientific records. The mechanism sharply distinguishes itself from mechanical capture.

assessments.operationalization: Monitor Silurus aristotelis nests continuously, identify parent sex, and measure guarding duration and attacks on small fishes. Male guarding lasting forty to fifty days supports the full claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species reproductive behavior and source literature

obstacles: Open continuous nest records for this endemic species are limited.
Guarding duration may vary with temperature and development.
assessments.rationale: Sex, guarding and duration are clear variables, and species accounts can test occurrence. Public data likely cover few nests, limiting the exact duration and generality.

assessments.operationalization: Classify diets and movement ranges of Mediterranean fishes, testing the near-universal carnivory assertion and whether carnivores move farther than non-carnivores. Herbivorous or omnivorous counterexamples directly refute universality.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish trophic level, diet, habitat and movement information

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open aquatic-animal tracking datasets

obstacles: Wander most requires a selected movement metric.
Diet varies by life stage.
assessments.rationale: Fish diet is comprehensively represented in FishBase and can resolve the universal statement quickly. Comparative movement data are less complete, but adequate to test the second clause for a broad subset.

assessments.operationalization: Code ink discharge in cuttlefish, octopuses and squid by context: predator threat, prey approach and background concealment. Non-threat concealment in octopus or squid refutes cuttlefish uniqueness.
obstacles: Fear is an inferred internal state.
The same event can serve both defense and concealment.
Behavioral coverage is uneven among cephalopods.
assessments.rationale: Contexts and ink release are observable, and existing videos and experiments can find counterexamples. Inferring exclusive motivation weakens discrimination, so only the contextual behavioral portion is resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify Octopus vulgaris skin color relative to adjacent substrate during prey approaches and alarm events. Reduced color distance in both contexts supports the claim.
obstacles: Camouflage includes texture and pattern as well as average color.
assessments.rationale: Dynamic camouflage is directly quantifiable from existing experimental and field imagery. The two stated contexts can be compared with standard image analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Compile hatch-to-death records for Octopus vulgaris and post-spawning changes in female feeding, activity and mass. Survival beyond one year or absence of post-spawning decline tests the respective clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated animal longevity records

obstacles: Wild lifespan is harder to measure than captive lifespan.
As a rule needs a chosen population proportion.
assessments.rationale: Cephalopod lifespan and post-reproductive senescence are standard life-history variables with extensive records. Existing data can resolve both the typical lifespan and female decline.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze surface video of Argonauta argo in wind, tracking web deployment, arm position and movement relative to wind and current. Wind-driven acceleration with web deployment supports sailing; submerged propulsion refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: OBIS
candidate_datasets.role: georeferenced argonaut observations

obstacles: Rare offshore surface behavior has little systematic video.
Currents confound apparent wind propulsion.
assessments.rationale: The mechanical prediction is clear and existing observations can assess arm and web use. Public data are too sparse and uncontrolled for a comprehensive hydrodynamic test.

assessments.operationalization: Use developmental and anatomical imaging to locate silk glands and spinnerets, determine whether hatchlings produce silk, and trace thread material from internal glands to body surface. Internal gland origin refutes the bark-like mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public spider anatomical specimens and scans

obstacles: Off the body could merely describe the visible exit point rather than material origin.
assessments.rationale: Spider silk anatomy and juvenile spinning are extensively documented and directly observable. Modern imaging cleanly discriminates external shedding from secretion by internal glands.

assessments.operationalization: Track individually marked honey bees for complete foraging bouts and identify each visited plant taxon by video, pollen or DNA. Any mixed-species trip refutes the absolute claim; the proportion of flower-constant trips tests its typical form.

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: bee-plant visitation interaction records

obstacles: Most visitation datasets do not retain trip-level sequences.
Flower identification from mixed pollen can be imperfect.
assessments.rationale: Flower constancy is a standard measurable behavior with substantial experimental literature. Existing open interaction data lack complete trip structure, so universality is only partly resolvable without targeted raw records.

assessments.operationalization: From hive videos and colony records, quantify queen killing and royal-cell destruction relative to queen number and impending swarming. Increased destruction when no swarm occurs supports regulation, but not workers' stated fear.
obstacles: Aristotle's kings must be mapped to queens.
Fear and intent are not directly measurable.
Hive-management practices alter queen replacement.
assessments.rationale: Queen elimination and cell destruction are observable and can be related to colony fission. Existing records can test the behavioral association, while the intentional explanation remains underdetermined.

assessments.operationalization: Record sting retention, tissue avulsion and survival after honey-bee workers sting substrates of differing elasticity. Death associated with a retained barbed sting and abdominal rupture supports the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public insect anatomical imaging relevant to sting morphology

obstacles: Bees can sometimes withdraw stings from other insects and survive.
assessments.rationale: The anatomy, injury and survival outcome are directly observable and extensively documented. Existing evidence can also resolve the scope conditions under which the claim holds.

assessments.operationalization: Age-mark worker bees and record task allocation and hair wear through life. Age-related shifts toward or away from foraging, plus measured setal abrasion, directly test each clause.
obstacles: Hairiness may reflect wear rather than indoor exposure.
Colony needs can reverse normal age polyethism.
assessments.rationale: Worker age and task are standard variables in honey-bee experiments with abundant existing data. The direction stated is sharply testable, as is the proposed morphology association.

assessments.operationalization: Video-record bees departing in high versus low wind and identify any deliberately carried stones, then measure flight stability with and without ballast. Repeated high-wind flights without stones refute the generalization.
obstacles: No known public dataset records carried-object identity and wind simultaneously.
Pollen or debris could be mistaken for stones.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is unusually concrete and highly discriminable, but ordinary bee datasets do not measure it. A decisive assessment needs new high-speed field observations.

assessments.operationalization: Mark workers and queens in Vespula and Polistes colonies and estimate overwinter survival and refuges. Worker survival into spring refutes the universal worker-death clause; queen recovery underground supports overwintering.
obstacles: Polistes and Vespula differ in colony cycle.
Winter non-detection alone does not prove death.
assessments.rationale: Social-wasp colony cycles and caste survival are standard, well-studied life-history outcomes. Existing observations and experiments can resolve the main claim across the named genera.

assessments.operationalization: For identified lions involved in livestock or human attacks, compare age, dental condition and hunting performance with non-conflict lions. Enrichment of old, dentally impaired individuals supports the proposed pathway.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank Data Repository
candidate_datasets.role: open lion movement data that can characterize livestock-area incursions

obstacles: Attack databases rarely include dental exams.
Habitat loss, prey depletion and opportunity confound age effects.
assessments.rationale: Attack, age and tooth condition are measurable, and some case series exist. Public linked records are incomplete and observational confounding prevents a clean universal causal conclusion.

assessments.operationalization: Analyze elephant swimming observations and respiratory anatomy, testing whether submerged animals keep the trunk tip in air and move air through it. Trunk occlusion or alternative breathing would refute the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public elephant anatomical imaging

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public wildlife video of elephant aquatic behavior

assessments.rationale: The anatomical airway and snorkeling behavior are directly visible and extensively documented. Existing images, videos and anatomy provide a decisive test.

assessments.operationalization: Follow hens before and after winning fights against cocks, measuring crowing, mounting, comb and tail morphology and spur growth, while recording age and ovarian status. Trait changes specifically following victory support the claim.
obstacles: Hormonal aging or ovarian disease can masculinize hens independently of fighting.
Public longitudinal fight-linked data are scarce.
assessments.rationale: All phenotypes are measurable, and existing poultry reports can test their occurrence. The asserted causal trigger is strongly confounded and lacks adequate public longitudinal data.

assessments.operationalization: Compare castrated and intact cocks by age at procedure for comb color, crowing, mating and male-trait development. Consistent loss or prevention after verified gonadal ablation supports the claim.
obstacles: Cauterizing the rump may not reliably castrate birds.
Historical procedure differs from modern caponization.
Open individual-level datasets are limited.
assessments.rationale: Androgen-dependent traits are explicit and many poultry experiments exist. The exact described intervention is ambiguous, so current data resolve hormonal castration better than cauterization itself.

assessments.operationalization: Compare voice pitch, androgen-dependent hair and baldness in men with documented prepubertal castration versus matched intact men. Any later hair, voice lowering or baldness refutes the corresponding absolute.
obstacles: Relevant historical cohorts are small and sensitive.
Age at castration and hormone treatment are often undocumented.
Never goes bald requires long follow-up.
assessments.rationale: The phenotypes are standard clinical variables and historical eunuch cohorts provide evidence. Public individual-level data are limited, and modern hormone treatment complicates a definitive universal test.

assessments.operationalization: Follow stags castrated before and after antler growth, recording antler initiation, size and annual casting against intact controls. Any antler growth after early castration or shedding after late castration refutes the absolutes.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public deer skeletal morphology records

obstacles: Castration timing and longitudinal antler histories are rarely open.
Antler response depends on season relative to the testosterone cycle.
assessments.rationale: The intervention and outcomes are precise, and veterinary or deer-farm studies provide partial evidence. Existing open data likely do not cover enough timing conditions for the full prediction.

assessments.operationalization: Code rumination and upper-incisor presence across mammal species and calculate their association and exceptions. Ruminants with upper incisors or non-ruminants lacking them determine the limits of the rule.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open comparative animal traits and source references

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public skull and dentition scans

obstacles: A few acknowledged exceptions make the exact decision threshold important.
assessments.rationale: Dentition and rumination are standard species traits with broad comparative coverage. Public anatomy and natural-history records permit a straightforward phylogenetic contingency analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Compare season-dated photographs and recordings within bird species for plumage color and song features. Repeatable within-individual or population seasonal shifts support the general claim; the blackbird example can be assessed separately.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: season-dated bird photographs, video and audio

obstacles: Age and molt can be confounded with season.
The historical owsel may not map exactly to Turdus merula.
assessments.rationale: Large public media archives contain the needed dates, colors and vocalizations. Standard image and acoustic analyses can test many species and the stated example.

assessments.operationalization: Compare morphology, genomes, banded individuals and seasonal occurrences of robin versus redstart and garden warbler versus blackcap. Distinct genomes and simultaneous populations refute seasonal transformation.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public sequence data for the four bird species

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public DNA barcode records

obstacles: Ancient names must be mapped carefully, though the proposed modern pairs are explicit.
assessments.rationale: Species identity and seasonal presence are exceptionally well covered by genetic and occurrence data. Multiple independent analyses decisively distinguish transformation from separate migratory species.

assessments.operationalization: Code dust- and water-bathing events by species, locomotor ecology, habitat and talon morphology from public videos and species accounts. Counterexamples test each categorical association.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: public bird bathing-behavior media

obstacles: Absence of bathing in media is not evidence of absence.
Crooked versus straight talons needs a morphological rule.
assessments.rationale: Positive bathing observations are plentiful and can refute universal exclusions. Systematic behavior coverage across the broad bird groups is incomplete, limiting confirmation.

assessments.operationalization: No observation can rank final cause as metaphysically prior to motor cause without first adopting Aristotle's causal framework.
obstacles: Priority among kinds of cause is a conceptual claim.
No unique measurable consequence distinguishes it from rival causal vocabularies.
assessments.rationale: This is a methodological and metaphysical ordering of explanations, not a biological prediction. Scientific datasets can describe mechanisms and functions but cannot settle the asserted ontological priority.

assessments.operationalization: Use embryological time series to determine whether vertebrae arise by patterned segmentation before fetal contortion or by fracture of a continuous backbone. Observed somitic segmentation without breakage refutes Empedocles' mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public vertebrate embryological and anatomical imaging

obstacles: The broader denial that animal characters are incidental is too sweeping, but the vertebral example is direct.
assessments.rationale: Modern embryology records the temporal origin of vertebral segmentation and sharply discriminates patterned development from accidental breakage. Existing imaging resolves the stated example directly.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate parent-offspring resemblance and genetic transmission for specified traits using pedigrees and genomes, while separating inherited from environmental effects. Heritable resemblance supports the claim; no parental predictive contribution would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: public genomic sequences across animals

candidate_datasets.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genotype-trait association data, especially in humans

obstacles: Certain characters is unspecified.
Parent phenotype alone does not establish a developmental mechanism.
assessments.rationale: Inheritance and parent-offspring resemblance are represented by enormous public genomic and pedigree resources. The general wording is broad, but many explicit trait operationalizations can directly test its core.

assessments.operationalization: Locomotion can be measured, but 'intellect' has no species-neutral operational definition that preserves the categorical claim; cognitive task performance tests narrower abilities only.
obstacles: Intellect is undefined and anthropocentric.
No finite behavioral battery establishes absence of intellect.
Different cognitive capacities yield conflicting classifications.
assessments.rationale: Animal cognition datasets can compare memory, planning or problem solving, but none resolve the philosophical category asserted here. The human-only boundary changes with the chosen proxy, so the claim as stated lacks a discriminating empirical criterion.

assessments.operationalization: Measure respiratory airflow, core and respiratory-tract temperature and heat exchange through breathing cycles across air-breathing animals. If airflow persists without the predicted heat alternation or is driven by pressure-generating muscles and gas demand, the stated necessary mechanism is refuted.

candidate_datasets.name: AnimalTraits
candidate_datasets.role: open metabolic-rate measurements and source references across terrestrial animals

obstacles: Heat discharge may be an effect of ventilation rather than its driver.
Coverage is richer for mammals and birds than other air breathers.
assessments.rationale: Respiratory mechanics, temperature and metabolism are standard physiological measurements with extensive public records. Temporal and intervention evidence can distinguish thermal driving from rival muscular and chemical-control mechanisms.

assessments.operationalization: Code wings and flight behavior across ant species and castes. Verified winged flying reproductives and wingless workers within ants directly confirm that the group spans both categories.
obstacles: Flight status differs mainly by caste and life stage rather than species.
assessments.rationale: Winged reproductive ants and wingless workers are directly documented in extensive public collections. The classification point is decisively testable with standard morphology and observation.

assessments.operationalization: Map each named kind to domestic taxa and their wild conspecific, feral, or ancestral populations, then test whether every kind contains both tame and wild members. A documented kind lacking any wild population would refute the near-universal statement.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts describing domestication, behavior, and wild distributions

obstacles: Tame, wild, feral, and ancestral wild populations are not equivalent categories.
The Indian dog example is taxonomically and historically ambiguous.
assessments.rationale: The named examples and tame/wild contrast are measurable, but substantial category interpretation is required. Public occurrence and species-account data cover the examples unevenly and cannot by themselves establish behavioral tameness for individual records.

assessments.operationalization: One could compare classifications produced by multivariate clustering with successive binary splits against accepted animal phylogenies, but no empirical threshold determines which grouping mankind instinctively recognizes or which classification animals should use.
obstacles: The claim is normative about proper classification.
Natural group and instinctive recognition lack unique measurable criteria.
assessments.rationale: Phylogenetic and trait data could compare algorithms, but could not settle the stated prescription without choosing a definition of naturalness in advance. Almost any result can be accommodated by changing the selected differentiae or similarity criterion.

assessments.operationalization: Encode homologous and analogous anatomical characters for birds and fishes, then test whether within-class variation is exclusively quantitative while between-class correspondences are exclusively analogous. Any within-class qualitative absence or novel structure refutes the strict claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: ontology-linked vertebrate anatomical phenotypes and homology-relevant characters

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: comparative three-dimensional anatomy of bird and fish specimens

obstacles: Degree versus kind is partly dependent on character coding.
No database exhaustively covers soft and hard anatomy across both classes.
assessments.rationale: The universal exclusivity can be tested for many coded structures, and counterexamples would be informative. Existing resources are taxonomically and anatomically incomplete, while the analogy judgment requires specialist homology decisions.

assessments.operationalization: Across mapped animal clades, code respiratory organs, circulating fluids, and their gas-transport or nutrient-transport functions. Test whether every lungless or bloodless group has a distinct structure or fluid performing the asserted corresponding office.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: comparative anatomical phenotype records for vertebrate organs

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: reviewed accounts of respiratory and circulatory anatomy across animal groups

obstacles: Bloodless animals spans many unrelated invertebrate phyla.
Analogy and same office require functional judgments not consistently encoded.
assessments.rationale: Respiratory structures and circulating fluids are observable, but the asserted analogies are interpretive. Public comparative resources can resolve selected clades, not the full scope of all animals.

assessments.operationalization: Functions and structure-function adaptation can be measured for particular parts, but no observation distinguishes a body made for a soul from the same body produced without that final cause.
obstacles: Soul and made for are not measurable biological variables.
The final-cause explanation adds no distinguishing prediction.
assessments.rationale: Individual organ functions are empirical, but the universal teleological relation is not. Existing anatomy data would document adaptation without testing the asserted direction of purpose.

assessments.operationalization: Code tissues and organs by material composition and test whether heterogeneous organs perform the listed actions while homogeneous tissues compose them. The further assertion that tissues exist for organs has no separate observable criterion.

candidate_datasets.name: Uberon
candidate_datasets.role: cross-species anatomical partonomy linking tissues, organs, and body parts

obstacles: Homogeneous and heterogeneous do not map cleanly to modern tissue categories.
The final-cause component is not discriminating.
assessments.rationale: Modern anatomical ontologies can test the compositional portion for many taxa. They cannot resolve why one class of parts exists, so only a restricted empirical component is resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Use lesion, recording, and anatomical evidence to locate neural control of sensation, voluntary movement, and nutrition across vertebrates and representative invertebrates. candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
candidate_datasets.role: sex-linked and other congenital phenotypes across animal species

candidate_datasets.name: Orphadata
candidate_datasets.role: human rare congenital disorder epidemiology

obstacles: 'Defective' is broad, historically loaded, and lacks a unique modern variable.
Animal surveillance is not comparable to population-level human registries.
assessments.rationale: Sex differences can be calculated for defined defect categories, and human data are strong. The unspecified phenotype and weak cross-animal surveillance make the universal contrast only partly resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Compare sex-specific fetal developmental milestones or maturity at equal gestational age, age at puberty, age at peak adult performance, and survival or biological aging. The full claim requires slower prenatal female development but earlier female puberty, prime, and aging.

candidate_datasets.name: CDC WONDER
candidate_datasets.role: sex-stratified fetal, birth, and mortality outcomes

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: sex, age, pubertal-development, anthropometric, and health measures

candidate_datasets.name: Human Mortality Database
candidate_datasets.role: sex-specific mortality schedules across populations and time

obstacles: 'Prime of life' and 'old age' admit multiple operational definitions.
Prenatal developmental speed is multidimensional rather than a single variable.
assessments.rationale: Large open human datasets resolve puberty and age-related outcomes with high precision, and fetal development can be tested with defined milestones. Interpretation is needed for 'prime' and overall developmental speed, but plausible operationalizations are testable now.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate menstruation resumption and conception rates during breastfeeding, then compare milk production before and after conception. Any menstruation or conception during lactation refutes the categorical clauses, while longitudinal milk-volume changes test the drying-up prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: National Survey of Family Growth
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive histories, pregnancy intervals, and breastfeeding variables

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys Program
candidate_datasets.role: large public survey datasets on breastfeeding, postpartum amenorrhea, and birth intervals

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: longitudinal studies of lactation during pregnancy and milk production

obstacles: Milk volume during a subsequent pregnancy is less widely measured than amenorrhea and conception.
Breastfeeding intensity strongly confounds both outcomes.
assessments.rationale: Large public reproductive surveys directly measure lactation, postpartum amenorrhea, and pregnancy timing. Standard survival or event-history analyses can resolve the categorical claim and quantify exceptions; milk cessation needs supplementary cohorts.

assessments.operationalization: Code fetal presentation at natural delivery across viviparous species and test whether head-first is universal or predominant. Any species in which normal births are routinely posterior-first refutes the universal, while fetal mass distribution data can separately test the proposed explanation.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: obstetric and veterinary studies reporting fetal presentation by species

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open supplementary datasets from comparative reproductive studies

obstacles: No known single dataset harmonizes fetal presentation across viviparous animals.
Clinical records overrepresent difficult births.
The causal weight explanation needs different anatomical data.
assessments.rationale: Birth orientation is directly observable and counterexamples are decisive. Human and domestic-animal data are plentiful, but the stated scope spans diverse viviparous taxa and available records are fragmented.

assessments.operationalization: Compare validated maximum longevity and adult survival across humans, elephants, and other animals. A credibly documented non-elephant species exceeding human maximum lifespan refutes the ranking.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated maximum longevity records across animal species

candidate_datasets.name: Human Mortality Database
candidate_datasets.role: validated human mortality and longevity data

candidate_datasets.name: COMADRE Animal Matrix Database
candidate_datasets.role: open demographic matrices and survival data for animal populations

obstacles: Maximum records are sensitive to validation and captive-versus-wild sampling.
Unequal observation effort biases species maxima.
assessments.rationale: Longevity is standardized in large comparative databases, and the ranking can be checked directly. Sampling bias affects interpretation but does not prevent decisive counterexamples or a well-supported comparison.

assessments.operationalization: Fit phylogenetic models of gestation length using neonatal mass, adult mass, lifespan, placental type, and developmental state, then compare the independent predictive contribution of offspring size and lifespan. Strong size effects persisting after covariate control support the observable causal prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation, body mass, offspring mass, and life-history traits

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation, longevity, and body-size variables across mammals

obstacles: Comparative correlations cannot uniquely establish Aristotle's developmental mechanism.
Offspring size, adult size, developmental state, and lifespan are evolutionarily correlated.
assessments.rationale: Existing comparative data can test whether offspring size statistically explains gestation better than lifespan. Serious phylogenetic and life-history confounding prevents the analysis from identifying a single 'real cause'.

assessments.operationalization: Compare recorded gestation ranges for Equus species, humans, and elephant species with the stated one-year, ten-month maximum, and two-year values. Species ranges containing or contradicting those values directly resolve each clause.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: curated gestation lengths for horses, asses, humans, and elephants

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: independent comparative mammalian gestation values

obstacles: Ancient months may be lunar rather than modern calendar months.
Species and individual gestation ranges must not be reduced to a single mean.
assessments.rationale: These are direct, standard life-history variables for well-studied species. Multiple open comparative databases provide sufficient coverage and the numerical assertions can be checked in days.

assessments.operationalization: No observation of eye-colour variation distinguishes absence of a final cause from an empirically identical material or efficient account unless an independent measurable definition of final causation is supplied.
obstacles: Final causation has no independent measurable criterion here.
The proposed alternatives can accommodate the same observed colour distribution.
assessments.rationale: Eye colour itself is measurable, but the claim concerns which metaphysical kind of cause applies. Without a distinct prediction for final causation, datasets cannot confirm or refute the stated distinction.

assessments.operationalization: Define fetal sleep and wake states from validated heart-rate, movement, and neurophysiological criteria, estimate time in each state, and compare with newborn sleep duration. Predominant fetal sleep with brief wake states and predominant newborn sleep supports the descriptive portions.

candidate_datasets.name: PhysioNet
candidate_datasets.role: open physiological time-series collections, including fetal and neonatal recordings usable for state classification

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: fetal behavioral-state studies across humans and oviparous animals

obstacles: Fetal 'sleep' is inferred and criteria differ by developmental stage and species.
The claimed causal link to newborn sleep is not isolated by descriptive data.
Broad animal coverage is limited.
assessments.rationale: Human fetal and neonatal state recordings can test a restricted, modernized version. They cannot establish a uniform pattern across animal embryos or that fetal sleep causes newborn sleep.

assessments.operationalization: Code synchronized video and sleep-state recordings of newborn facial behavior for laughter-like vocalizations and crying while awake versus asleep. Any unambiguous awake laughter refutes the categorical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Databrary
candidate_datasets.role: research video library containing developmental and infant behavior recordings

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: neonatal smiling, laughter, crying, and sleep-state studies

obstacles: Neonatal smiles, reflex vocalizations, and laughter require explicit coding criteria.
Accessible videos may not represent the immediate newborn period or synchronized sleep state.
assessments.rationale: Behavioral outcomes and a decisive counterexample are clear. Public video and sleep resources can test subsets, but a purpose-built representative newborn dataset linking vocal behavior to state is not evident.

assessments.operationalization: Measure iris colour from calibrated longitudinal images at birth and later infancy in humans and comparable animal cohorts. Any newborn lacking bluish irises refutes the human universal; documented colour changes and animal neonatal changes test the remaining clauses.

candidate_datasets.name: Databrary
candidate_datasets.role: publicly discoverable longitudinal infant video suitable for coded eye-colour observations where resolution permits

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: longitudinal infant iris pigmentation studies and veterinary comparisons

obstacles: Lighting and camera white balance make retrospective colour coding unreliable.
Birth images and later follow-up are rarely linked in open datasets.
Cross-animal neonatal iris data are sparse.
assessments.rationale: The universal human assertion is easy to refute with calibrated counterexamples, but suitable open longitudinal colour data are limited. The cross-animal clause greatly exceeds current standardized coverage.

assessments.operationalization: Compile verified heterochromia records by species and quantify eye-colour diversity within species. A confirmed heterochromic individual of any nonhuman, nonhorse animal refutes the exclusivity clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
candidate_datasets.role: curated animal pigmentation and heterochromia phenotypes

obstacles: Photographic artefacts and eye disease can mimic congenital heterochromia.
Absence of observations cannot rank eye-colour diversity across all animals.
assessments.rationale: The exclusivity assertion has decisive, photographically verifiable counterexamples and public phenotype resources. The superlative claim that horses have the greatest variety would require a systematic animal-wide sampling design not present in current data.

assessments.operationalization: Compare standardized photopic and scotopic visual-acuity or contrast-sensitivity tests among people grouped by measured iris pigmentation, controlling age, refractive error, ancestry, and ocular disease. Opposite colour effects in day and night conditions would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: public visual-acuity, ophthalmic, demographic, and health measurements for human participants

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: studies and supplements linking iris pigmentation with glare, acuity, and dark adaptation

obstacles: Large population datasets may lack both iris colour and scotopic testing.
Ancestry and ocular pigmentation covary with several visual and environmental factors.
assessments.rationale: The hypothesis maps to standard vision tests, but no single named open cohort clearly contains iris colour plus matched day and night performance. Existing studies permit partial tests with meaningful confound control.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate cataract and clinically defined night-blindness prevalence by iris pigmentation, controlling age, ancestry, UV exposure, diabetes, and inherited retinal disease. Opposing excess risks in light- and dark-eyed groups would support the two-part claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: population ophthalmic examinations, visual function, and relevant health covariates

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public association summaries for iris pigmentation and ocular-disease phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: epidemiological studies of iris pigmentation, cataract, and night blindness

obstacles: Nyctalopia is a symptom with heterogeneous causes.
Iris colour is strongly associated with ancestry and UV exposure.
Open cohorts may not contain all variables jointly.
assessments.rationale: Both outcomes have modern clinical definitions and substantial public ophthalmic data. Joint individual-level data on pigmentation and both diagnoses are incomplete, and confounding limits causal interpretation.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify eye prominence or orbital depth from specimens and pair it with species-level distance acuity measured under comparable conditions. A negative association between prominence and long-distance acuity after controlling eye size and ecology would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public 3D specimen media for quantifying orbit and eye placement

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts for ecology and sensory adaptations

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: species-specific visual-acuity measurements

obstacles: Eye prominence has no standard cross-species measure.
Comparable behavioral acuity data exist for relatively few species.
Eye size, retinal anatomy, and ecology are major confounders.
assessments.rationale: A measurable comparative test is possible after substantial interpretation. Morphology and acuity data are stored separately and have narrow, biased taxonomic overlap, so only selected taxa can be assessed.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect anatomical descriptions and specimen images for external pinnae versus external auditory openings in Phocidae. Consistent absence of pinnae with patent ear canals supports the anatomical claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public specimen images and 3D anatomical media for seals

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: public taxon accounts describing phocid external anatomy

obstacles: The ecological 'because' clause is harder to identify causally than the anatomy.
True seals must be distinguished from eared seals.
assessments.rationale: External pinnae and auditory openings are directly observable in abundant public descriptions and media across true seals. The anatomy is fully resolvable now, though aquatic causation would require a broader comparative evolutionary analysis.

assessments.operationalization: Code age-associated loss of hair or coat pigmentation from longitudinal or age-known individuals across mammals, including humans and horses. Clear visible greying in another species refutes the near-exclusive assertion.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: species aging context and longevity for comparative sampling

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: veterinary and comparative reports of age-related depigmentation

obstacles: Age is usually unknown in wildlife photographs.
Seasonal coat change and individual markings can mimic greying.
Animal-wide absence cannot be established from opportunistic records.
assessments.rationale: Visible depigmentation can be coded and counterexamples can resolve the exclusivity claim. Existing open images lack reliable ages for most animals, so systematic cross-mammal prevalence is only partially available.

assessments.operationalization: Use longitudinal scalp photographs or clinical records to map the first region of patterned hair loss and first region of greying in men. Temporal or clinical evidence of temporal or occipital balding onset would refute the universal negative.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: clinical studies and supplements on male-pattern alopecia and spatial patterns of canities

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public phenotype association records for male-pattern baldness and hair greying

obstacles: Most cohorts record severity classes rather than the first affected location.
Longitudinal greying-location datasets are uncommon.
Alopecia subtypes other than androgenetic alopecia complicate 'no one'.
assessments.rationale: Anatomical onset regions are objective and categorical counterexamples are decisive. Public genetic and clinical evidence covers common patterns, but the necessary longitudinal spatial phenotype is not consistently available.

assessments.operationalization: Measure hair curvature in geographically sampled populations and model it against long-term local temperature and humidity while controlling ancestry. An independent moist-cold association with straighter hair and hot-dry association with curlier hair would support the environmental portion.

candidate_datasets.name: WorldClim
candidate_datasets.role: open historical temperature and precipitation layers for population locations

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public association summaries for hair morphology traits

obstacles: No identified open global dataset jointly measures individual hair curvature and lifelong climate exposure.
Genetic ancestry and climate are highly confounded.
The brain-dryness mechanism lacks a validated measurable counterpart.
assessments.rationale: The geographic correlation can be operationalized but would be difficult to distinguish from population history and genetics. Existing climate and genomic resources provide only components, and the proposed brain mechanism is not resolved by them.

assessments.operationalization: Link sea-urchin specimens with collection depth and temperature, measure test size and spine length or hardness, and model trait differences across depth within species. Small bodies with disproportionately large, hard spines in cold deep water support the pattern.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media for test and spine morphometrics

candidate_datasets.name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS)
candidate_datasets.role: marine occurrence records with environmental and depth context

obstacles: Hardness is rarely recorded in specimen databases.
Morphology, depth, temperature, and species identity are confounded.
Sixty fathoms may not correspond to a biologically uniform deep-water class.
assessments.rationale: Depth, body size, and spine dimensions are measurable, and marine occurrence plus specimen media provide a viable restricted analysis. Spine hardness and causal attribution to cold are much less available.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate clinically defined scalp hair-loss prevalence and pattern in women, intact men, and castrated or androgen-deprived men. Documented female or eunuch baldness refutes the categorical claim; group differences test its weaker empirical implication.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: population health and examination data for sex-stratified hair-loss analyses where available

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genetic association records for alopecia phenotypes

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: clinical cohorts of female-pattern hair loss and androgen-deprived patients

obstacles: 'Bald' could mean androgenetic alopecia specifically or any alopecia.
Historical eunuch cohorts are small and not representative.
Castration status is uncommon in open population data.
assessments.rationale: Female alopecia is well documented and can decisively refute the universal wording. The eunuch comparison and Aristotle's seminal-secretion explanation require specialized cohorts and remain only partially testable.

assessments.operationalization: In longitudinal records, compare time to greying between consistently covered and uncovered scalp regions or between habitual hat wearers and matched non-wearers, controlling age, ancestry, smoking, and sun exposure. Earlier greying under coverage would support the prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: searchable epidemiological literature on canities and environmental risk factors

obstacles: Habitual hat exposure and region-specific greying are not standard cohort variables.
Hat use is confounded by sun exposure, occupation, culture, and existing hair loss.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is measurable with longitudinal exposure and pigmentation data. No known public dataset jointly records hat use, covered scalp regions, and greying onset, so a credible test needs new targeted data.

assessments.operationalization: Search taxonomically verified observations and specimen records for wholly or extensively white individuals of partridges, ravens, sparrows, and bears, excluding normally white species, seasonal coats, and photographic artefacts. One validated case in each named group confirms occurrence.

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals (OMIA)
candidate_datasets.role: curated pigmentation phenotypes in animal species

obstacles: Leucism, albinism, seasonal whitening, and overexposure must be distinguished.
The causal phrase 'development is perverted' is not independently tested by occurrence records.
assessments.rationale: Rare white phenotypes are conspicuous, verifiable, and represented in large public image and phenotype repositories. The occurrence claim is resolvable now even though Aristotle's causal characterization is vague.

assessments.operationalization: Measure drinking-water temperature and longitudinal hair pigmentation in genetically and environmentally comparable cattle or goats. A dose-dependent whitening under warm water and darkening under cold water, reversible or replicated across herds, would support the mechanism.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: searchable animal nutrition and coat-colour literature for any existing intervention studies

obstacles: Water temperature is not a standard livestock phenotype or exposure variable.
Hair colour is dominated by genotype, age, season, and nutrition.
Observational climate comparisons would not isolate drinking water.
assessments.rationale: A controlled or well-instrumented longitudinal test is straightforward in principle. No known public dataset records water temperature and coat-colour change together, making new experimental or farm data necessary.

assessments.operationalization: For animals with patterned coloration, compare calibrated ventral-belly luminance with dorsal and lateral homologous regions from standardized images. Any reliably darker underside supplies a counterexample to the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: specimen media with multiple anatomical views

obstacles: Opportunistic images are not colour-calibrated and often omit the belly.
Defining 'not uniformly coloured' and homologous regions across taxa requires judgment.
Animal-wide universality cannot be confirmed from sampled taxa.
assessments.rationale: Modern image repositories make a broad counterexample search feasible and colour contrast is quantifiable. Coverage and photographic standardization are insufficient to confirm a universal across all nonuniform animals.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate fundamental frequency from sex-identified adult vocal recordings within species, then compare female-minus-male pitch across taxa and specifically in cattle. Higher female pitch generally and lower cow pitch would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: publicly accessible animal sound archive with taxonomic metadata

candidate_datasets.name: Xeno-canto
candidate_datasets.role: open wildlife sound recordings, especially birds

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open bioacoustic datasets with sex and individual metadata

obstacles: Sex is absent from many recordings.
Call type, age, context, and recording quality affect pitch.
Comparable cattle recordings by sex may require literature supplements.
assessments.rationale: Fundamental frequency is directly measurable from extensive public bioacoustic data. Metadata and taxonomic biases limit a general animal-wide estimate, but many species and the alleged cattle exception can be tested.

assessments.operationalization: Inspect bovine cardiac anatomy records, necropsies, and images for an os cordis and verify mineralized structures histologically or radiographically. Any confirmed occurrence in a bull supports the existential claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public anatomical and CT media that can show mineralized cardiac structures

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: veterinary anatomical and histological reports of bovine os cordis

obstacles: The structure may be cartilage or age-related mineralization rather than mature bone.
Specimen repositories may not record sex consistently.
assessments.rationale: This is an existential anatomical claim, so a single well-documented bull specimen is sufficient. Public veterinary reports and imaging resources can provide decisive histological or radiographic evidence.

assessments.operationalization: For species with pre- and post-castration recordings, quantify fundamental frequency and compare post-castration values with intact males and females; separately define and measure specific behavioral traits rather than 'female character'. Female-like shifts would support restricted components.

candidate_datasets.name: Macaulay Library
candidate_datasets.role: animal vocal recordings potentially including managed or altered individuals

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: human and veterinary castration studies reporting voice and behavior

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open supplementary behavioral and bioacoustic data

obstacles: 'Female character' has no single objective definition.
Pre/post-castration recordings with female controls are rare.
Effects depend strongly on species and age at castration.
assessments.rationale: Voice pitch can be tested for selected species using standard acoustics, while the character clause requires substantial and potentially misleading interpretation. Available evidence is fragmented and cannot support the universal 'all animals'.

assessments.operationalization: Use developmental dental series for pigs and lions to identify deciduous and permanent homologues and which tooth classes are replaced. Replacement outside lion canines or documented pig tooth replacement refutes the respective clause.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: public juvenile and adult cranial CT scans and dental specimens

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species natural-history and anatomical accounts

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: veterinary and comparative dental-eruption studies

obstacles: 'Shed' must be distinguished from replacement, eruption, and wear.
Age-series specimen metadata may be incomplete.
assessments.rationale: Dental replacement is a standard anatomical trait in two well-studied mammals. Public specimen scans and veterinary literature provide age series sufficient to resolve both specific claims.

assessments.operationalization: No finite observation distinguishes a world in which nature never acts in vain 'so far as possible' from one containing failures, because any apparent counterexample can be redescribed as constrained possibility.
obstacles: 'In vain' and 'so far as possible' lack independent measurement criteria.
The qualification makes the universal resistant to counterexamples.
assessments.rationale: This is a teleological methodological assumption rather than a claim with a specified observable consequence. Its terms permit every biological outcome and therefore no dataset can discriminate it from rivals.

assessments.operationalization: Measure milk temperature at feeding and time to eruption of the first teeth in suckling mammals, controlling species, energy intake, growth, health, and maternal effects. Earlier eruption with hotter otherwise equivalent milk would support the prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: searchable neonatal nutrition and dental-eruption studies that may provide partial evidence

obstacles: Milk temperature is rarely retained as a measured exposure.
Temperature covaries with feeding method and milk handling.
Comparative tooth-eruption timing is not linked to individual feeding temperature.
assessments.rationale: The variables and intervention are clear, but existing public life-history data do not record milk temperature. A controlled animal study or purpose-built neonatal cohort appears necessary for a credible causal test.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate the age distribution of third-molar gingival eruption from population dental examinations and identify verified late-life eruptions. A central eruption age near twenty plus rare substantially later cases supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
candidate_datasets.role: public age-linked dental examination and tooth-status data

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: population dental-eruption studies and reports of delayed third-molar eruption

obstacles: Eruption, root growth, impaction, and delayed exposure after tooth movement must be distinguished.
Older adults with newly visible third molars are rare.
assessments.rationale: Third-molar eruption is routinely defined and recorded in dental examinations, with extensive age-stratified public data. Standard descriptive analyses can test the typical age, while literature cases address the late-age tail.

assessments.operationalization: Any part that divides into pieces like itself is uniform by the definition given, and any part that does not is composite, so there is no separate measurement that could confirm or refute the division.
obstacles: The uniform versus composite split is fixed by how the parts are defined, not by a comparative measurement.
assessments.rationale: The statement sorts parts by a logical criterion rather than reporting a quantity, a presence, or a comparative pattern. Tissue images and anatomical atlases can illustrate flesh and hands, but they cannot disagree with a rule that labels each part by how it divides. Nothing in a dataset would count as a counterexample without changing the definition.

assessments.operationalization: Score each named pair (bone and fish bone, nail and hoof, hand and claw, feather and scale) for shared tissue and developmental origin versus functional resemblance only; shared identity would count against 'only by analogy', and mere functional likeness would count for it.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Curated anatomical characters linking vertebrate structures, including bone, scales, feathers, and keratinous appendages, across taxa.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: Specimen media for bone, hoof, feather, and scale structure in the named groups.

candidate_datasets.name: GEISHA
candidate_datasets.role: Chicken gene-expression and anatomical context for the developing feather as one side of the feather-scale comparison.

obstacles: Analogy versus sameness has several competing operationalizations.
Fish-bone can be read as spine, fin ray, or bone tissue, and those readings need not agree.
assessments.rationale: The examples can be proxied by histology and developmental origin, which Phenoscape and imaging repositories record for some of the structures. Aristotle's own contrast, same versus merely analogous, is not a variable in those sources, and more than one modern criterion would draw the line in a different place. A test can examine the pairs, not decide the classificatory principle as he framed it.

assessments.operationalization: Map the gadfly to candidate insect groups with aquatic larvae, then test whether those larvae develop in fresh water and the adult lives on land; a group whose larvae never leave water, or whose adults are aquatic, would refute that reading.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Life-cycle accounts for horse flies and other insects whose larvae live in wet sediment and whose adults are terrestrial.

obstacles: The Greek oistros is not securely identifiable to one modern genus.
Several insects with aquatic larvae fit a loose reading and would fail a stricter one.
assessments.rationale: Life-cycle accounts and observation records can test an aquatic-larva to terrestrial-adult sequence once a taxon is chosen. The name itself is disputed, and different identifications (tabanids versus other mud-dwelling larvae) do not share one life history. Existing data can test particular mappings, not the sentence under every plausible mapping at once.

assessments.operationalization: Treat crooked talons as membership in the raptorial orders and gregariousness as checklist counts above a flock threshold in eBird; counts consistently near one would support the claim, and repeated large flocks or colonial roosts would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: eBird
candidate_datasets.role: Checklist counts for hawks, falcons, vultures, and owls, used as a flock-size measure.

candidate_datasets.name: EltonTraits 1.0
candidate_datasets.role: Diet and foraging stratum to mark raptorial birds independently of the flock counts.

candidate_datasets.name: AVONET
candidate_datasets.role: Species-level morphology and primary lifestyle for the same birds, as context for which species are aerial predators.

obstacles: Gregarious can mean a feeding flock, a roost, or a breeding colony.
Crooked talons are inferred from raptorial orders, which also include species with weaker feet.
assessments.rationale: eBird records the count variable directly, and diet tables can restrict the test to birds of prey. The morphological phrase and the social word both need a threshold the text does not give, so the analysis tests a stated proxy rather than a single coded trait. Within that proxy, large vulture or falcon counts would be enough to reject a universal ban on flocks.

assessments.operationalization: For each domesticated form in DAD-IS, ask whether IUCN and occurrence-backed taxonomies still list a wild counterpart of the same lineage; a domesticated kind with no wild counterpart, living or historically attested, would refute the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: FAO DAD-IS
candidate_datasets.role: Inventory of domesticated breeds, including horse, cattle, pig, sheep, goat, and dog.

candidate_datasets.name: IUCN Red List
candidate_datasets.role: Extinction and wild-status assessments for the proposed wild progenitors.

candidate_datasets.name: ASM Mammal Diversity Database
candidate_datasets.role: Current species list for wild and domestic mammals, used to keep the name matching explicit.

obstacles: The same kind is ambiguous once domesticates are ranked as separate species.
Several wild progenitors are extinct, so a present-day survey does not match the claim's timeframe one for one.
assessments.rationale: Breed inventories and extinction assessments cover the named livestock and many other domesticates. What they do not settle by themselves is whether aurochs and cattle, or wolf and dog, are the same kind, which is the decision the sentence requires. The named examples can be checked; the universal depends on that taxonomic choice and on extinct populations that are not in living-occurrence tables.

assessments.operationalization: Code urinary bladder and intestine as present or absent across animals that have a gut or an excretory organ; any species with a urinary bladder and no intestine would refute the implication, and species with an intestine and no bladder would confirm the 'not conversely' clause.

candidate_datasets.name: Phenoscape Knowledgebase
candidate_datasets.role: Presence and absence of excretory and digestive structures curated from the comparative literature.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Species accounts stating whether a urinary bladder and an intestine are present, including birds and fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish anatomy for intestine and renal structures, keeping the swim bladder separate from a urinary bladder.

obstacles: Bladder presence is not a column in the main life-history tables and has to be compiled.
A swim bladder or other air space can be mistaken for a urinary bladder.
assessments.rationale: The implication is a clean presence-absence contrast, and birds are an obvious intestine-without-bladder case already written into species accounts. Coverage across all animals with excretory organs is incomplete in the curated anatomy sources, so the test is solid for vertebrates and thin outside them. A full survey would be a literature compilation rather than a query of one trait matrix.

assessments.operationalization: For each phylum, score mechanoreception, vision, hearing, and chemoreception as present or absent; the claim holds if every animal lineage with any sense has mechanoreception and at least one lineage lacks each other sense.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Sensory descriptions for representative animals across phyla, including eyeless and earless species.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: Zebrafish sensory anatomy as a worked vertebrate case with touch, vision, hearing, and smell.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: A phylum-level tree so that gaps in sensory coverage can be counted rather than ignored.

obstacles: Touch is difficult to score in animals without neurons, especially sponges.
No public dataset inventories every sensory modality for every phylum.
assessments.rationale: Model-animal anatomy and species accounts can show that vision, hearing, and smell fail to be universal and that mechanoreception is widespread in animals with nervous systems. They do not contain a modality matrix for the whole animal kingdom, and sponges make the word sense itself unstable. The claim is testable on the groups with described sense organs and open at the base of the tree.

assessments.operationalization: Map blooded to vertebrates and bloodless to invertebrates, then compare walking-leg number; a vertebrate species with more than four legs would refute the claim, and invertebrates restricted to zero, two, or four legs would weaken the grouping.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: Body-plan accounts giving leg number and circulatory type for arthropods and vertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: Vertebrate versus invertebrate placement for the species being counted.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: Leg-bearing marine invertebrates, including crustaceans, with body-size and taxonomic context.

obstacles: Bloodless has to be mapped to the absence of vertebrate blood, and some invertebrates have haemoglobin.
Leg number is not a single open column across phyla.
assessments.rationale: Leg number and the vertebrate circulatory plan are standard facts in species accounts, so the main pattern can be checked without new collecting. The Aristotle word does not match a single laboratory variable, because haemoglobin and leg-like appendages occur outside the intended groups. The result is a partial test of a mapped version of the sentence, not a direct query.
